clue.text: Setting-off place in Devon

definitions.meaning: a place to set off from, the start of a journey
a headland on the south coast of the English county of Devon, near Dartmouth

explanation.surface: A traveller names the Devon spot where the journey begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is where you start; as a proper name it is a headland in Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a starting spot for any journey, and the name of a Devon headland with a lighthouse.

clue.text: Hardy girl gets involved in these cliques

indicators.note: gets involved suggests the letters of the name become entangled into a new order

parts.note: Tess is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: A Hardy heroine joins a few exclusive circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy girl' looks like a sturdy girl, but means Thomas Hardy's heroine Tess; 'gets involved' rearranges her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets of people are groups or circles, much like cliques.

clue.text: Acquit Jack and find the right answer

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, and so is an AB, able seaman
to solve is to find the right answer

explanation.surface: A defendant named Jack is cleared once the puzzle is worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to clear or free them from blame.

clue.text: Hobo has cooking-vessel mainly used as carrier

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp
a steamer is a pan for cooking food by steam

explanation.surface: A vagrant carries a pan around, mostly to haul things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' looks like 'mostly', a sign to drop letters, but means 'on the main', at sea: the answer is a cargo ship without a fixed route.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo vessel taking freight wherever it is offered sails the seas as a carrier.

clue.text: Cause excessive suspense to pheasant or beetle

definitions.meaning: game birds are hung to mature; hang one too long
to beetle is to jut out or project, as beetling brows or cliffs do

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper keeps a pheasant or an insect hanging too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspense' is literal: the hanging of game. 'beetle' is not the insect but the verb meaning to project.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging game too long is to hang it to excess, and a jutting cliff projects over what lies below.

clue.text: Landor's first love

parts.note: the poet Walter Savage Landor wrote '... I loved, and next to ..., Art'

explanation.surface: Asking who a poet's first sweetheart was.
explanation.walkthrough: It is not a person: Landor's line 'Nature I loved, and next to Nature, Art' names his first love.
explanation.definitionFit: Landor's quatrain 'Dying Speech of an Old Philosopher' places the natural world first among the things he loved.

clue.text: Hold up the post somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of post are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: The mail has been delayed in some unexplained way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges POST; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something up is to halt or block it.

clue.text: Harley Street describes the summit

parts.note: the summit is the top
London's street of doctors: MO, a medical officer, plus ST for street

explanation.surface: A London address of medical consultants depicts a mountain peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Harley Street is London's famous street of private doctors, giving MO (medical officer) and ST (street). As a whole the answer is the word that describes the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest part is the uppermost, the word applied to a peak.

clue.text: Stall-holder appears to be inquisitive about a bender, oddly enough

indicators.note: about means around, so the nosy word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to be inquisitive is to pry

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters of a bender come out in a strange arrangement

explanation.surface: A market trader seems nosy about someone's drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' rearranges A BENDER to EBENDAR, and 'about' puts PRY round it. A stall here is a cathedral seat, held by a canon.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon who holds a cathedral benefice has his own stall, or seat, in the choir.

clue.text: Handing down instruments new and old

definitions.meaning: wills are legal documents by which property is handed down
the two halves of the Christian Bible, Old and New

explanation.surface: A list of tools, some new and some old, is being passed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instruments' suggests tools, but here it means legal documents; the second definition names the two parts of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will is a legal deed passing on property, and the Bible's two divisions carry the same name.

clue.text: Handy fencing implement

parts.note: reads like a useful garden tool for putting up fences, but means a sword held in the hand for the sport of fencing

explanation.surface: A useful tool for building a garden fence.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the sword used in one of the three Olympic fencing disciplines, gripped in the hand.

clue.text: At 104 the Italian menial is a state official

parts.note: CIV is 104 in Roman numerals
il is Italian for 'the'
a menial is a servant

explanation.surface: An Italian servant aged 104 turns out to be a government employee.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text lost the 1 of 104; the printed page reads 104.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the civil service is a government employee.

clue.text: Cut short wool-gathering

definitions.meaning: the amount of wool shorn from sheep in a season

explanation.surface: Daydreaming is interrupted abruptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wool-gathering' usually means daydreaming; here it is taken literally, the gathering of wool by shearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim is to snip, and a season's shearing of fleece is also called by that word.

clue.text: Nebuchadnezzar was such a beastly vegetarian

definitions.text: Nebuchadnezzar was such a beastly vegetarian

parts.words: Nebuchadnezzar was such a beastly vegetarian
parts.note: in the Book of Daniel the Babylonian king was driven out and ate grass like an ox, a plant-eater like an animal

explanation.surface: An ancient king was an unpleasantly strict vegetarian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like an insult but means 'like a beast': the king grazed on grass as cattle do.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass-eating animal is a plant-eater, which is what the king became in his madness.

clue.text: Hare-brained chap shows off paces to cricketing doctor

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of paces are knocked out of order

parts.note: Dr W. G. Grace, the great Victorian cricketer, was a medical doctor

explanation.surface: A silly fellow shows off his stride to a cricket-playing doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges PACES into SCAPE; W. G. Grace was England's famous bearded cricketer and a qualified doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or reckless ne'er-do-well is a feckless fellow.

clue.text: Producing GCE in art, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters of the fodder are scrambled

explanation.surface: A student gets an art exam pass by whatever means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges GCE and IN ART together. The GCE was the British school-leaving exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing something is making or bringing it into being.

clue.text: Boy and girl sang in rhythm

parts.note: Lil is a girl's name, short for Lillian
Ted is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A young couple sang together keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the boy first, but in the answer the girl's name comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To lilt is to sing or speak with a light, swinging cadence.

clue.text: A river and the French sailor's guiding light

parts.note: the Po is a river of northern Italy
les is French for 'the' (plural)
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A river, some French people and a seaman navigate by a light.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern star has long been used by navigators to steer.

clue.text: Track an Afghan tribesman

parts.note: a track is a path

explanation.surface: Following the trail of a man from an Afghan tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pathans, or Pashtuns, are a people of Afghanistan and north-west Pakistan.

clue.text: Swinging bar patronized by bold youth

definitions.meaning: a horizontal bar hung on ropes for acrobats
the song 'The Daring Young Man on the Flying ...'

explanation.surface: A lively pub frequented by brash young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging bar' suggests a fashionable pub, but means a bar that swings; the second part alludes to the music-hall song about a daring young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus apparatus is a bar hung from ropes, and the old song's daring young man flew on one.

clue.text: Reckon to make a hundred on the side, right?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman wonders whether to score a century as a sideline.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text inserts a stray '22'; the printed page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to think over or judge, as in weighing a matter up.

clue.text: Like a computer this is a drug

indicators.note: this stands for the answer itself, which with is added makes the drug, so is must be taken away

parts.note: digitalis is a heart drug made from foxglove

explanation.surface: A drug that makes the user behave like a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this is a drug' says the answer followed by IS spells the drug DIGITALIS, a heart medicine from foxglove.
explanation.definitionFit: Computers work with numbers held as discrete digits.

clue.text: " Drink deep, or taste not the --n spring" (Pope)

definitions.text: Drink deep, or taste not the --n spring" (Pope)

parts.words: Drink deep, or taste not the --n spring" (Pope)
parts.note: Pope's Essay on Criticism: 'A little learning is a dangerous thing'; the blank plus N names the Muses' spring

explanation.surface: A quotation from Alexander Pope with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap so that with the printed N it makes the adjective; the answer is the region of Macedonia sacred to the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: The district of ancient Macedonia held sacred to the Muses gives its name to their spring of learning.

clue.text: Rumour rife in the Bordeaux area

definitions.meaning: gossip spread by word of mouth, as in 'heard it on the ...'
the climbing plant of the vineyards is everywhere around Bordeaux

explanation.surface: Gossip spreads widely around the French wine region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rife' pretends to describe rumour spreading, but it belongs to the second definition: the plant grows everywhere in Bordeaux wine country.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay travels by the informal network named after a vine, and vines cover the claret country of south-west France.

clue.text: In which not only poor students disport themselves

definitions.text: In which not only poor students disport themselves

parts.words: In which not only poor students disport themselves
parts.note: the poor wear tattered clothes, and British students hold charity carnival weeks under the same name

explanation.surface: A description of how hard-up students amuse themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag in British universities is an annual student charity stunt week; tattered clothing worn by the poor has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn-out clothes are worn by the poor, and students' charity festivities carry the same name.

clue.text: Rams are awkward weapons

indicators.note: being awkward suggests the letters of rams fall into a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: Male sheep make clumsy weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are awkward' rearranges RAMS. Battering rams were weapons, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, as in a call to arms.

clue.text: Strange name that stuck in Macbeth's throat

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of name are changed into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd word that the murderer could not bring himself to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges NAME. In Shakespeare's play Macbeth, after the murder, cannot say the word ending a prayer: it 'stuck in my throat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth tells his wife he could not pronounce the closing word of the prayer said by the sleeping grooms.

clue.text: Instrument with extensive capabilities

parts.note: really a semicircular device for measuring angles

explanation.surface: A tool that can do a great many things.
explanation.walkthrough: To protract is to draw out or extend, so the geometry tool's name sounds like a thing that lengthens.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a geometry tool for drawing and measuring angles, whose name contains a verb meaning lengthen.

clue.text: They see to the passing of the motion, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt, a sound-alike

parts.note: in a debate a motion is passed when the votes in favour, the ayes, have it

explanation.surface: Members attend to getting a proposal through the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: the votes for a motion in Parliament, the ayes, sound like the organs of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are what see.

clue.text: False accounts, produced by Rita, safely camouflaged

indicators.note: camouflaged means disguised, so the letters of Rita and safely are concealed in a new order

explanation.surface: Rita has cooked up a misleading story but disguised it well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camouflaged' rearranges RITA and SAFELY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Made-up stories, or lies, are often called by the name of children's magical stories.
